title: Some Movies That Changed Filmmaking
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss films that changed filmmaking, working through a list: Battleship Potemkin (1925) and the Odessa Steps montage, Buster Keaton's stunts and deadpan style, The Jazz Singer (1927) and synchronized sound via Vitaphone, Citizen Kane (1941) and its non-linear storytelling, deep focus, low angles and lighting, Breathless and the French New Wave with jump cuts, Fellini's 8 1/2 and surrealism, Toy Story (1995) as the first all-CGI feature, and Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) with its match cut, silence, and production secrecy. Also covers Tintin CGI, Interstellar comparisons, a listener mail correcting the scientific law vs. theory distinction, and a Birdman discussion.

segments.title: Opening banter and last studio episode
segments.summary: Hosts chat about Roger Ebert documentary, watching movies on planes, and that this is the last episode in the old office before moving.

segments.title: Battleship Potemkin and the Odessa Steps montage
segments.summary: Discussion of Battleship Potemkin (1925) as a propaganda narrative, its Soviet montage theory and Odessa Steps sequence, and its influence on later films like The Untouchables, Godfather, and Raiders. Also a correction about Fatty Arbuckle.

segments.title: Buster Keaton's stunts and deadpan
segments.summary: Keaton's dangerous stunts such as the falling house, and his deadpan style contrasted with Chaplin; influence on later deadpan comedians.

segments.title: The Jazz Singer and early synchronized sound
segments.summary: The Jazz Singer (1927) as the first feature with substantial spoken dialogue, using Vitaphone discs synced to projectors; its box office and ineligibility for Best Picture.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short transition to a break before the next segment.

segments.title: Citizen Kane and storytelling innovations
segments.summary: Citizen Kane (1941) and its non-linear narrative, deep focus by Gregg Toland, off-center framing, expressionistic lighting, Welles' theater background, the wipe, and low angle shots with ceilings.

segments.title: Film noir and Fritz Lang tangent
segments.summary: Hosts try to recall the director of a moody noir film with an innovative lighting style, mixing up names; they mention Hitchcock and Fritz Lang.

segments.title: French New Wave and jump cuts
segments.summary: The French New Wave's handheld, flat, indie-style filmmaking, exemplified by Breathless; critics turned filmmakers; jump cut editing and its use in Goodfellas and Soul Taker.

segments.title: Fellini's 8 1/2 and surrealism
segments.summary: 8 1/2 as a film about filmmaking that kicked off surrealist filmmaking, its traffic-jam opening influencing Falling Down and R.E.M.'s video, and its influence on Gondry, Aronofsky, Lynch, Gilliam.

segments.title: Jingles and Toy Story
segments.summary: Thanks to the jingle musicians, then Toy Story (1995) as the first all-CGI feature and its influence on later animation, the decline of cell animation, and the Animated Feature Oscar category.

segments.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
segments.summary: Kubrick's 2001 (1968) discussed as innovative in visuals and sound, its thirty-minute silent openings and endings, the Clarke collaboration, Sagan consultation on aliens, and Kubrick's destruction of sets and footage.

segments.title: Interstellar, Prometheus, and Kubrick comparisons
segments.summary: Hosts debate whether Interstellar and Prometheus are Kubrickian, comparing explanation and ambiguity in films, and mention Inception and The Sixth Sense.

segments.title: 2001 structure, match cut, and Kubrick's obsessiveness
segments.summary: Breakdown of 2001's three movements, the bone-to-satellite match cut and its nuclear warhead meaning, Kubrick's meticulous set decoration, the Room 237 documentary, and alternate titles.

segments.title: Movie podcast wrap-up
segments.summary: Hosts mention related past episodes and the site's archive search.

segments.title: Listener mail on scientific law vs. theory and Birdman discussion
segments.summary: Listener Mike DuPont corrects the hosts that theory is more developed than law; Chuck responds. Hosts then discuss Foxcatcher and Birdman.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Contact info for the show and sign-off.
